requirement: `UsageStats::tools` starts empty and holds one entry per invoked tool, keyed by name. This includes built-in and registered tools.
rationale:
structural: The requirement text is "`UsageStats::tools` starts empty and holds one entry per invoked tool, keyed by name. This includes built-in and registered tools."

The only structural obligation is the shape of the field. `tools` must be a collection keyed by tool name, and it must start empty. A `Vec<ToolUsage>` or a flat list with no name key would give the same results for some callers but would not be "keyed by name". `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph.rs#struct[UsageStats]` declares `pub tools: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, ToolUsage>`, which is keyed by a `String` name. The struct also derives `Default`, so the map starts empty. Both points are visible in the struct, and the struct is the supplied root. It is also marked `{impl}` for this requirement.

The remaining clauses are observable behavior, not structure. These are "one entry per invoked tool" and "includes built-in and registered tools". Many implementations could record usage and still meet them. The test criterion covers them, not this one. A different map type, such as `HashMap`, would also satisfy the text, so the choice of `BTreeMap` is discretionary. No further implementation roots are needed.

behavioral: The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[registered_tools_use_the_current_context_and_ordinary_node_ids]` covers every obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.by_name`.

- **Starts empty:** `assert!(domain.cache().usage().tools.is_empty())` runs before any ask.
- **One entry per invoked tool, keyed by name:** after `ask`, the test asserts that `stats.tools.keys()` is exactly `["inspect","lookup_requirements","submit_result"]`.
  - `lookup_requirements` is called twice and still has a single key, so repeated calls do not add entries. The test also checks `stats.tools["lookup_requirements"].calls == 2`.
  - `read_node`, `outgoing_edges` and `get_next_page` are offered to the model but never invoked. They are absent from the keys, so entries exist only for invoked tools.
- **Registered and built-in tools:** `inspect` and `lookup_requirements` are registered through `with_tool`. `submit_result` is built in. All three appear, keyed by name.

The test does not invoke every built-in tool. The requirement draws no distinction among built-ins, so I treat built-in coverage via `submit_result` as sufficient. I found no unacknowledged gap.
